Great Masters, Graces, shavepates, Sons of the Harpy

Yunkai.summary:
Yunkai, also called the Yellow City, is one of the Slaver Cities on the eastern coast of Slaver's Bay in central Essos. Ruled by the Wise Masters, Yunkai's main export is bed slaves. It is said to be a disreputable place. Yunkai is also referred to as the queen of cities, a title also claimed by Qarth. Yunkai is a rival of Astapor and Meereen, but the cities are not enemies.

The Yunkish emblem is a variation on the harpy of Old Ghis: a woman's torso, wings of a bat instead of arms, legs of an eagle, and a scorpion's tail. Its talons grasp a whip and an iron collar.

Astapor.summary:
Astapor, dubbed the Red City, is the southernmost of the Slaver Cities on Slaver's Bay. The city is renowned for their training of the Unsullied, eunuch slave soldiers. Astapor is a rival of Yunkai and Meereen, but the cities are not enemies.

The Astapori emblem is a variation on the harpy of Old Ghis: a woman's torso, a bat's wings instead of arms, an eagle's legs, and a scorpion's tail. In its talons hangs a chain with open manacles at either end.

Plaza of Pride, Plaza of Punishment, pyramid of Nakloz, pyramid of Ullhor, Douquor's Pit, Jothiel's Pit, Temple of the Graces

Yaros.summary: Yaros is an island in the east of Slaver's Bay. To the northeast is Yunkai and to the south Astapor, both on the mainland.

Hesh.summary: Hesh is a city located in the Lhazar region of Essos. It is northwest of Lhazosh and west of Kosrak. A trade route from Hesh extends through the Khyzai Pass to Meereen.

Kosrak.summary: Kosrak is a city located in the Lhazar region of Essos. It lies on a tributary of the Skahazadhan river, to the east of Hesh and to the northeast of Lhazosh. A trade route from Kosrak extends southeast through the red waste to the ruined city of Vaes Tolorro, while another route heads northeast to Adakhakileki.

Lhazosh.summary: Lhazosh is a city in the Lhazar region of Essos. It is located southeast of Hesh and southwest of Kosrak. A trade route from Lhazosh extends southeast through the red waste to the ruined cities of Vaes Orvik and Vaes Shirosi.

Lhazar.summary:
Lhazar is an area of the semi-arid lands south of the Dothraki sea. A region of pastures and hills, it is inhabited by the Lhazareen, a people of sheepherders, and in the southern parts by Ghiscari. There are three cities in Lhazar, Hesh, Lhazosh, and Kosrak. The Skahazadhan passes through northern Lhazar.

Lhazar borders the Dothraki sea to the north and Slaver's Bay to the south. It is connected to Meereen via the Khyzai Pass in the sandstone mountains.

The Skahazadhan.summary: The Skahazadhan is a major river of central Essos.

Krazaaj Has.summary: Krazaaj Has is a ruined city in Essos between the southeastern Dothraki sea and Lhazar. It is located on a tributary of the eastern Skahazadhan, west of Vaes Mejhah and east of Meereen. It was originally called Ghardaq, but was ruined by the Dothraki after the Doom of Valyria. It is now known by its Dothraki language name, Krazaaj Has, meaning "Sharp Mountains" after its Ghiscari pyramids.

Vaes Mejhah.summary: Vaes Mejhah is a ruined Ghiscari city in Essos between the southeastern Dothraki sea and Lhazar. It is located on a tributary of the eastern Skahazadhan, between Vaes Efe and Krazaaj Has. It was ruined after the Doom of Valyria, and its Dothraki language name means City of Whores.

The Black Cliffs.summary: The Black Cliffs are a series of cliffs that are situated on the northwest coast of Slaver's Bay, south of the Painted Mountains. They lie between Tolos and the ruined city of Bhorash, south of the Demon Road.

The Poison Sea.summary: The Poison Sea is a large inland saltwater sea at the northeastern edges of the red waste. The ruined city of Adakhakileki lies at the northern tip of the sea. Northeast of the Poison Sea is Vaes Jini and the Stone Road. The eastern side of the sea abuts part of the Bone Mountains. Many leagues south of the Poison Sea lies Qarth. The Dothraki consider the sea poisonous because their horses cannot drink the saltwater.

Adakhakileki.summary: Adakhakileki is a ruined city that lies at the northern edges of the red waste in Essos, on the northernmost shore of the Poison Sea, not distant from the Stone Road. Vaes Jini is northeast of the city. Adakhakileki is located in the foothills of the western Bone Mountains. Little is known of its inhabitants, although its Dothraki language name means "The Cannibals".

Vaes Jini.summary:
Vaes Jini is a ruined city in Essos, located on the Stone Road in the foothills of the western Bone Mountains. It was originally called Yinishar and was inhabited by people related to those of Samyriana, but it is now known by its Dothraki name, Vaes Jini, meaning "City of Goats". It was once located along the Silk Road.

Southwest of Vaes Jini is the ruined city of Adakhakileki and south is the Poison Sea. To the northwest is the edge of the Dothraki sea.

Samyriana.summary: Shamyriana or Samyriana is a fortified city in Essos, located on the Stone Road in the eastern Bone Mountains, near the Great Sand Sea.

Bayasabhad.summary: Bayasabhad, also known as the City of Serpents, is a fortified city in Essos, located on the Sand Road in the eastern Bone Mountains, near the Great Sand Sea.

The Red Waste.summary: The red waste or Red Waste, also called the red lands, is a region of Essos west of the Bone Mountains. The desert is a barren and unforgiving landscape of stunted trees, devilgrass, and ancient ruins.

The Dry Bones.summary: The Dry Bones is a name sometimes applied to the southern Bone Mountains, in central Essos. Located east of the red waste and west of the Great Sand Sea, they are so-named because water is sparse there. They do not seem to have the snowcapped mountains of the northern Bones, which are called the White Mountains (Krazaaj Zasqa) due to their snow cover. The Dry Bones are scoured by sandstorms (apparently from the red waste), which carve the mountains into strange shapes.

Vaes Tolorro.summary:
Vaes Tolorro is the name given by Daenerys Targaryen and her followers to an abandoned city in the red waste beyond the Dothraki sea. Vaes Tolorro means "the city of bones" in the Dothraki language.

The original name of Vaes Tolorro is unknown. It is possible this was one of the city-states established by the Qaathi.

Vaes Shirosi.summary: Vaes Shirosi is a ruined town located in Essos, north of Qarkash and Port Yhos, in the southwestern portion of the red waste. The Qaathi town was destroyed by the Dothraki during the Century of Blood. Its Dothraki language name means City of Scorpions.

Vaes Qosar.summary: Vaes Qosar is a ruined Qaathi city located in Essos, east of Qarkash and northwest of Qarth, in the southeastern portion of the red waste. It was originally called Qolahn, but it is now known by its Dothraki language name, Vaes Qosar, meaning City of Spiders, after its destruction by the Dothraki during the Century of Blood.

Vaes Orvik.summary: Vaes Orvik is a ruined city located in Essos, north of Port Yhos, in the southwestern portion of the red waste.

Port Yhos.summary: Port Yhos is a town in Essos located southeast of Slaver's Bay on the shores of the Summer Sea. The westernmost settlement controlled by Qarth, it is south of Vaes Orvik and southwest of the red waste. Qarkash is to the east of Port Yhos.

Qarkash.summary: Qarkash is a Qartheen town in Essos, located east of Slaver's Bay on the shores of the Summer Sea. It is south of the red waste and west of Qarth and the ruins of Qolahn. Port Yhos is to the west of Qarkash.

Qarth.summary: Qarth is an ancient port city located on the southern coast of Essos. It has been referred to as the Queen of Cities, a title also claimed by Yunkai in Slaver's Bay.
facts: House of the Undying, Hall of a Thousand Thrones, Temple of Memory, triple wall, port
Thirteen, Tourmaline Brotherhood, Ancient Guild of Spicers, Sorrowful Men, warlocks

Qal.summary: Qal is an island in the east of the Jade Gates, south of the Bone Mountains of Essos. Qal is fortified on its northwestern and southeastern coasts with Qartheen harbor cities.

Asabhad.summary: Asabhad is a city at the western boundary of Yi Ti in Essos along the shores of the Jade Sea, east of the Bone Mountains. It is located at a forested river mouth. Situated on a trade route connecting Qarth and Yin, Asabhad is where many caravans begin their journey to the Mountains of the Morn.

Ghiscar.summary: Ghiscar is a region of southern Essos located on the eastern coast of the Gulf of Grief. Old Ghis is found within this region. Astapor and the Worm River are north of the Ghiscari hills. South of Ghiscar are the Ghiscari Strait and some islands, including the large island Ghaen and a small island with the city of New Ghis.

Old Ghis.summary: Old Ghis is a ruined city in Essos. It is located in southwestern Ghiscar, east across the Gulf of Grief from the Valyrian peninsula. It was the capital city of the Old Empire of Ghis. The ancient city was one of the oldest known cultures and nations in the world. Its founding and golden age predate that of its successor, Valyria, by thousands of years.

Ghaen.summary: Ghaen is an island in the Gulf of Grief. It borders the Ghiscari Strait and lies off the southern coast of Essos near Ghiscar. South of it are two smaller islands, including New Ghis.

New Ghis.summary: New Ghis is an island city in the Gulf of Grief, which borders on the Summer Sea. Its island lies south of Ghaen. Ghiscar and the ruins of Old Ghis are located to the north, past the Ghiscari Strait. A city dependent on slavery, New Ghis is a much smaller port than Volantis.
facts: Island in the Gulf of Grief

The Ghiscari Strait.summary: The Ghiscari Strait is a strait between Ghiscar in southern Essos and the island of Ghaen. It flows from the Gulf of Grief into the Summer Sea.

Skull Island.summary:
Skull Island, also known as Skull Isle, is the northernmost of the Basilisk Isles. It is located in the Summer Sea north of Zamettar in Sothoryos. The small isle is windswept and uninhabited.

Many of corsairs of the Basilisks decorate the hulls and masts of their ships with severed heads. When the flesh has rotted off them, the corsairs replace the heads with fresh ones, while the bare skulls are delivered to Skull Isle as an offering to some dark god. The shores of the island are lined with skulls.

Ax Isle.summary: Ax Isle is the easternmost island of the Basilisk Isles, which are off the northern coast of Sothoryos. To the north lies New Ghis, across the Summer Sea.

Zamettar.summary: Zamettar is a ruined city on the northern coast of Sothoryos. It lies on a large delta, the mouth of the Zamoyos. To the north lies the Summer Sea and Ax Isle, to the west the bulk of the Basilisk Isles, and to the south, deep in the jungle, Yeen and, beyond, the Green Hell.

Yeen.summary: Yeen is a ruined city on the Zamoyos in the continent of Sothoryos. To the north is Zamettar at the river delta. Enormous apes are said to live in the forests south of Yeen.

Gorosh.summary: Gorosh is a ruined city on the northern coast of Wyvern Point in Sothoryos.

Wyvern Point.summary: Wyvern Point is a peninsula located in eastern Sothoryos. Named after the wyverns that hunt above its jungles and swamps, it contains the ruined penal colony Gorosh. Northeast of Wyvern Point is Lesser Moraq.

Lesser Moraq.summary: Lesser Moraq is a forested island in the eastern Summer Sea, west of Great Moraq and Vahar and northeast of the Cinnamon Straits. Lesser Moraq is located northeast of Wyvern Point in Sothoryos.

Great Moraq.summary: Great Moraq, the largest island in the known world, is located between the Summer Sea to the west and the Jade Sea to the east.

Faros.summary: Faros is a city at the mouth of a river on the northern stretch of Great Moraq's western coast. The inhabitants of the city worship the Stone Cow.

Port Moraq.summary: Port Moraq is a port city on the southern coast of Great Moraq, near the Cinnamon Straits. The land north of the city is a dense rain forest. South of Port Moraq is the Isle of Elephants. Traders often stop at the port when returning from the Jade Sea.

Vahar.summary: Vahar is a city on an island of the same name in the eastern Summer Sea. Vahar, located between Great Moraq to the east and Lesser Moraq to the west, has become wealthy from the spice trade.

The Cinnamon Straits.summary: The Cinnamon Straits separate Great Moraq from several islands to the south and west. Along with the Jade Gates north of Great Moraq, the Cinnamon Straits divide the Summer Sea and the Jade Sea. Vahar and Lesser Moraq are to the northwest of the Straits, while the Isle of Elephants is to the southeast. It is named after the cinnamon harvested from its isles.

The Isle of Whips.summary: The Isle of Whips is a small, isolated island in the Jade Sea, largely barren and named for its role as a way station for slavers. It is situated off the southern coast of Essos, east of Great Moraq and northwest of Marahai. Northeast of the Isle of Whips is Yi Ti in Essos.

The Isle of Elephants.summary:
The Isle of Elephants is an island in the Jade Sea south of Great Moraq and Port Moraq and southeast of the Cinnamon Straits. The city of Zabhad is located on its northern shore and is the only known settlement on the island. Northeast of the Isle of Elephants is Marahai.

According to records set down by Corlys Velaryon in his letters, the Isle of Elephants is ruled by a shan, who rules from a palace made of ivory. The island has numerous elephants.

Zabhad.summary: Zabhad is a city on the northern shore of the Isle of Elephants in the Jade Sea. It is the chief port of the island and is part of the trader's circle in the sea.

The Summer Sea.summary: The Summer Sea is a body of water located south of Westeros and Essos. The southern sea has deep blue waters and is warm from the sun.

The Worm.summary: The Worm or Worm River is a river in central Essos. Its headwaters begin in the hills north of Ghiscar and the city of Astapor lies near the river's mouth, where it flows into Slaver's Bay.

The Jade Gates.summary: The Jade Gates is a narrow strait which connects the Summer Sea and the Jade Sea, separating the great city of Qarth on the southern coast of Essos from the island of Great Moraq. The Cinnamon Straits is a similar passageway south of Great Moraq. Located in the east of the strait is the small island of Qal, which is fortified at each end with Qartheen harbor cities.

Sothoryos.summary: Sothoryos or Sothoros is one of the three known continents of the known world. It lies to the southeast of Westeros and is south of Essos across the Summer Sea. East of Sothoryos is the southern Jade Sea.

The Green Hell.summary: The Green Hell is a region in Sothoryos that lies beyond the forests south of the ruins of Yeen. It is said to be the home of beasts even more fearsome than those found in the northern area of the continent. There are reports of creatures such as pale white vampire bats that can drain the blood of a man in minutes, tattooed lizards that run down their prey and rip them apart with long curved claws on their hind legs, snakes fifty feet long, spotted spiders, and wyverns.

Lake Zamoyos.summary: The Zamoyos is a river in Sothoryos which flows into the Summer Sea at a large delta. It is known for its green waters, quicksands, and rotting, half-submerged trees. The river contains crocodiles, schools of carnivorous fish, and worms which lay eggs in swimmers.

Leviathan Sound.summary: Leviathan Sound is a large bay of the eastern Shivering Sea off the coast of northern Essos. It contains a few islands. The Howling Hills are to the southwest and the Plains of the Jogos Nhai are to the south. Leviathans mate and birth their young in Leviathan Sound.

The Thousand Islands.summary: The Thousand Islands are an extensive archipelago in the eastern Shivering Sea off the northern coast of Essos. To the southwest are the Plains of the Jogos Nhai, to the south are Nefer and N'Ghai, and to the southeast is Mossovy.

The Plains of the Jogos Nhai.summary: The plains of the Jogos Nhai are in Essos, east of the Great Sand Sea and the Howling Hills, north of Yi Ti and the Shrinking Sea, and west of N'Ghai and the Bleeding Sea. To the north is Leviathan Sound and the Shivering Sea.

Nefer.summary: Nefer, referred to by travelers as the Secret City, is the capital of N'ghai, and the kingdom's last remaining city. Nefer enjoys a sinister reputation as a haunt of necromancers and torturers.

N'Ghai.summary: N'ghai is a small kingdom in the Further East of Essos.

Mossovy.summary: Mossovy, also known as Far Mossovy, is a broad, forested region of northeastern Essos along the shore of the Shivering Sea. It is at the edge of the known world, east of N'Ghai and north of the Cannibal Sands and the Grey Waste. The Thousand Islands are found north of the grim, grey forest.

Cannibal Sands.summary: The Cannibal Sands are a pair of small deserts bordering the Grey Waste in the Further East of Essos.

The Grey Waste.summary: The Grey Waste is a vast desert in the Further East of Essos.

The Great Sand Sea.summary:
The Great Sand Sea is a massive desert valley and canyon in Essos, just east of the Bone Mountains and southeast of the Krazaaj Zasqa. The Steel Road skirts around the north of the Great Sand Sea, while farther to the north are the Howling Hills. Some maesters believe it to be an ancient inland sea, since dried, and become baking hot in the south and progressively colder to the north.

Cities between the Great Sand Sea and the Bone Mountains include Kayakayanaya just to the northwest, Samyriana in the central region, and Bayasabhad to the southwest. On the other side of the Great Sand Sea are Tiqui to the southeast and Trader Town between its center and the Shrinking Sea, on the opposite side as Samyriana. A number of these settlements were within the Patrimony of Hyrkoon, an ancient nation that flourished east of the Bone Mountains and had its heartland in the once fertile Great Sand Sea.

The Shrinking Sea.summary: The Shrinking Sea is in eastern Essos. It is east of the Great Sand Sea, north of Yi Ti, and south of the plains of the Jogos Nhai. Trader Town is to the west of the Shrinking Sea. The landlocked Shrinking Sea has drained over time and now is only a few lakes.

Trader Town.summary:
Trader Town is a rude, sprawling garrison city of northern Yi Ti in eastern Essos. The city lies east of the Great Sand Sea, and west of the Shrinking Sea. The vast plains of the Jogos Nhai are north of Trader Town. From Kayakayanaya, the Steel Road skirts the topmost northern edge of the Great Sand Sea, and turns south to Trader Town. The city is connected to Tiqui and Bayasabhad by the Sand Road.

Trader Town is the seat of General Pol Qo, Hammer of the Jogos Nhai, the self-proclaimed first orange emperor.

Tiqui.summary: Tiqui is a city in Yi Ti, located in the western hills of the region.

The Bleeding Sea.summary: The Bleeding Sea is a large inland sea in eastern Essos. It is named for its blood-red waters, which are caused by a blooming plant.

The Five Forts.summary: The Five Forts are massive fortresses along the northeastern boundaries of the Golden Empire of Yi Ti, situated between the Bleeding Sea and the Mountains of the Morn. Northeast of the Five Forts are the Land of the Shrykes, K'Dath, Bonetown, the Grey Waste, and the Cannibal Sands.

K'Dath.summary: K'Dath is a semi-legendary city supposedly located in a plain located in the Further East of Essos.

The Land of the Shrykes.summary:
The Land of the Shrykes is a plain in the Further East of Essos. It is bordered by the Bleeding Sea to the west, the Five Forts and the Mountains of the Morn to the south, Bonetown and the Dry Deep to the east, and K'Dath to the north.

The land is said to be a dangerous place populated by shrieking monsters.

Bonetown.summary: Bonetown is a rumored town in the Further East of Essos.

The Dry Deep.summary: The Dry Deep is an "L"-shaped canyon in far eastern Essos, south of the Cannibal Sands and the Grey Waste. The Dry Deep broadly runs east to west, with the Land of the Shrykes and K'Dath to the northwest. Just north of the Dry Deep is Bonetown, where strange, aged bones from the valley are traded. At its western end, the canyon narrowly runs south along the eastern side of the Mountains of the Morn. Southeast of the Dry Deep are the Cities of the Bloodless Men. It is said the valley is entirely devoid of water and life.

The Cities of the Bloodless Men.summary: Cities of the Bloodless Men are said to exist in the Further East of Essos. Their inhabitants are said to be a race of bloodless men.

The Mountains of the Morn.summary: The Mountains of the Morn are a mountain range in the Further East of Essos.

The City of the Winged Men.summary: The City of the Winged Men is a legendary city in far eastern Essos.

The Hidden Sea.summary: The Hidden Sea is a legendary sea nestled in the southeastern stretches of the Mountains of the Morn in far eastern Essos. The City of the Winged Men is located along the northwestern shore of the Hidden Sea, while Carcosa is situated at the southeastern corner. Southwest of the Hidden Sea are the Shadow Lands.

Carcosa.summary: Carcosa is a legendary city in far eastern Essos. It is located on the southeastern shore of the Hidden Sea within the Mountains of the Morn; the City of the Winged Men is situated on the northwestern shore. The sorceror lord claiming to be the 69th yellow emperor of Yi Ti lives in exile at Carcosa.

The Golden Empire of Yi Ti.summary: The Golden Empire of Yi Ti is a realm located in the eponymous region of the Further East of Essos. It is the supposed successor to the mythic Great Empire of the Dawn, which, according to legend, fell during the Long Night. It is ruled by a God-Emperor, who is worshiped as divine, though in the present day the God-Emperor has little actual power beyond the limits of the capital city.

The Jungles of Yi Ti.summary:
Yi Ti is a nation and region in Essos, east of Qarth and the Bone Mountains and bordered by the Jade Sea to the south. Nearby islands in the Jade Sea are Leng and the Isle of Whips. North of Yi Ti are the Great Sand Sea, the Shrinking Sea, and the Bleeding Sea; a great river runs south from the Bleeding Sea through Yi Ti to the Jade Sea. East of Yi Ti are the Mountains of the Morn, the Shadow Lands, and the city of Asshai. In the Common Tongue, things relating to Yi Ti are known as "YiTish".

The realm of the YiTish civilization is the Golden Empire of Yi Ti, which was, according to legend, preceded by the Great Empire of the Dawn. Maester Yandel speculates that the YiTish civilization was contemporary with the realm of the Fisher Queens, whereas the YiTish priests insist that mankind's first towns and cities arose along the shores of the Jade Sea, dismissing the rival claims of the Sarnori and Ghiscari as the boasts of savages and children.

Yin.summary:
Yin is the great port city of Yi Ti on the Jade Sea. It is connected by a trade route to Asabhad to the northwest. A river from the forests of Yi Ti leads south to Yin.

The dynasties of the grey, indigo, and pearl-white emperors ruled the Golden Empire of Yi Ti from their seats at Yin, and, in the present, the azure emperors have done the same.

Si Qo.summary: Si Qo, known as Si Qo the Glorious, was a city of the Golden Empire of Yi Ti, located in the heart of Yi Ti's jungle. Though now long fallen and overgrown, Si Qo was the capital of the Empire during the rule of the scarlet emperors, who raised it to be their capital.

Jinqi.summary:
Jinqi is a city in Yi Ti in southern Essos. It is located near a delta along the Jade Sea, north of Leng. The nearby river flows from the Bleeding Sea to the north.

The dynasty of the maroon emperors kept their martial court at this city, to better guard the eastern frontiers of the empire against reavers from the Shadow Lands.

Leng.summary: Leng is a large island in the Jade Sea, off the southern coast of Essos. To the north is the city of Jinqi in Yi Ti. East of Leng are the Shadow Lands, while to the south are the Manticore Isles. The island of Marahai is to the southwest. Leng is ruled by god-empresses.

Leng Yi.summary: Leng Yi is a city on the island Leng in the eastern Jade Sea. It is located on the northern shore of the forested island, southwest of Jinqi in Yi Ti.

Leng Ma.summary:
Leng Ma is a city on the island Leng in the eastern Jade Sea. It is located on the western shore of the forested island, near the mouth of a river.

Leng Ma and Leng Yi are reminiscent of YiTish cities like Yin and Jinqi.

Turrani.summary: Turrani is a city on the island Leng in the eastern Jade Sea. It is located on the southern shore of the forested island, near the mouth of a river and north of the Manticore Isles. Unlike Leng Yi and Leng Ma in the north, which were founded by men of Yi Ti, Turrani was founded by the original inhabitants of the island, the Lengii. It is a wealthy city rich in spices and gems.

Marahai.summary:
Marahai is a crescent-shaped island in the central Jade Sea, off the southern coast of Essos. West of Marahai are Great Moraq, the Isle of Whips, and the Isle of Elephants. Additionally, Leng and the Manticore Isles are east of Marahai. The city of Yin in Yi Ti is to the north across the Jade Sea.

Marahai is called a paradise isle. Within its curvature are two small volcanic isles which often emit smoke and flame.

The Manticore Isles.summary: The Manticore Isles are a group of seven small islands in the eastern Jade Sea, off the southern coast of Essos. The islands of Leng and Marahai are to the north and west, respectively. East of the Manticore Isles are Asshai and the Shadow Lands. The islands are named after the manticores that are said to be populous there.

The Jade Sea.summary: The Jade Sea is a large body of water in the Further East of the known world, beyond the Jade Gates, which separate it from the Summer Sea.

Ulos.summary: Ulos is a mountainous isle in the Saffron Straits between the Shadow Lands and Ulthos. An unnamed ruined city lies in the northern part of the isle. It is the easternmost island in the known world.

Asshai-by-the-Shadow.summary: Asshai is a mysterious port city in the far southeast of the known part of Essos, where the Ash river meets the Jade Sea at its eastern exit, the Saffron Straits. Asshai is on the southernmost edge of a mountainous peninsula known as the Shadow Lands, thus the city is often called Asshai by the Shadow or Asshai-by-the-Shadow. To go to Asshai can be described as to "pass beneath the shadow", and the area of the Shadow Lands and Asshai are sometimes referred to simply as the Shadow.
facts: About the same as a good-sized market town
As big as Volantis, Qarth, King's Landing, and Oldtown combined

Stygai.summary: Stygai, also known as the City of the Night, is a ruined city in the mountainous Shadow Lands of eastern Essos.
facts: Vale of Shadows, Shadow Lands, Essos

The Shadow Lands.summary: The Shadow Lands, also called the Shadow, is a mountainous area in the far east of Essos.

The Saffron Straits.summary:
The Saffron Straits are the eastern exit of the Jade Sea, dividing Essos and Ulthos. The city of Asshai is on the north side of its western entrance. North of the straits are the Shadow Lands, and Ulthos is to the south. The Saffron Straits widen to the east, and in them is the island of Ulos; then they run off east outside the known world.

According to a semi-canon source, the straits are named after the saffron carried over the water by traders.

Ulthos.summary: Ulthos is a landmass in the far east of the known world.

The Vale of Shadows.summary: The Vale of Shadows is a river valley in the Shadow Lands northeast of Asshai. The valley is a narrow cleft in the mountains through which the river Ash passes on its way from the Mountains of the Morn to the Jade Sea. The mountain cliffs are so high and steep that it is said no light falls within the valley except at noon. Demons and dragons and worse things are said to live in caves in the cliffs. At the heart of the valley is the ruined city of Stygai.

The Straits of Leng.summary: Leng is a large island in the Jade Sea, off the southern coast of Essos. To the north is the city of Jinqi in Yi Ti. East of Leng are the Shadow Lands, while to the south are the Manticore Isles. The island of Marahai is to the southwest. Leng is ruled by god-empresses.

King's Landing.summary:
King's Landing is the capital of the Seven Kingdoms, located in the crownlands on the east coast of Westeros. It is situated along the kingsroad at the mouth of the Blackwater Rush and overlooks Blackwater Bay. King's Landing is the site of the Iron Throne and the Red Keep, which is the seat of the king, Robert I from House Baratheon of King's Landing.

The main city is surrounded by a wall, manned by the City Watch of King's Landing, also known as the gold cloaks. King's Landing is the most populous city in Westeros, but unsightly and dirty compared to other cities. Poorer smallfolk build shanty settlements outside the city. The stench of the city's waste can be smelled far beyond its walls.

King's Landing's harbor, the principal port of the Seven Kingdoms, is rivaled only by Oldtown, which is larger in area but less populous. Nearby towns include Rosby and Duskendale to the northeast and Tumbleton to the southwest, while the kingswood is found south of the capital across the Blackwater. Driftmark and Dragonstone in the Gullet protect the bay from the narrow sea.

The demonym used for its inhabitants is "Kingslander".
facts: King of the Andals, the Rhoynar, and the First Men, Feudal society
King Robert I Baratheon (AGoT), King Tommen I Baratheon (ADwD)

Winterfell.summary: Winterfell is the ancestral castle and seat of power of House Stark and is considered to be the capital of the north. It is in the center of the northernmost province of the Seven Kingdoms, on the kingsroad that runs from Storm's End to the Wall. The castle is situated at the eastern edge of the wolfswood, north of the western branch of the White Knife and Castle Cerwyn. Winterfell is south of the northern mountains and southwest of Long Lake, one hundred leagues (three hundred miles) southeast of Deepwood Motte.
facts: Lord Eddard Stark (AGoT), Lord Ramsay Bolton (ADwD)
Great Hall, Great Keep, First Keep, broken tower, godswood, crypt, winter town

Ice River Clans.summary: The ice-river clans or ice river clans are clans of free folk who live near the great ice rivers beyond the Wall, north of the Frozen Shore and south of the Lands of Always Winter. They are said to feast on human flesh.

Cave-dwellers.summary: Cave dwellers or cave-dwellers are clans of free folk that live in the caverns of the Frostfangs, surrounding Thenn.

Nightrunner Tribes.summary: The Nightrunners are a clan of free folk who live beyond the Wall.

Hornfoot Tribes.summary: The Hornfoots are a clan of free folk who live beyond the Wall near the Frostfangs.

Forktop.summary: Forktop is one of the largest mountains in the Frostfangs. It is called Forktop due to its twin peaks.

The Antler.summary: The Antler River is a river found beyond the Wall. It is formed by at least two branches whose sources are in the northeast of the haunted forest. It flows southeast into the Shivering Sea.

Storrord's Point.summary: Storrold's Point is a peninsula beyond the Wall on the Shivering Sea. At its tip is Hardhome, a ruined free folk settlement. Crab gods are worshiped by some tribes who live along Storrold's Point.

Kingshouse.summary: Kingshouse is the seat of House Magnar on the island Skagos in the north.

Goldgrass.summary: Goldgrass is the seat of House Stout in the north.

The Long Lake.summary: Long Lake is a large lake in the north.

Broken Branch.summary:
The Broken Branch is a river in the southeastern lands of the north. The headwaters of the Broken Branch lie in the Sheepshead Hills, while Ramsgate sits at its mouth, near where the Bite meets the Shivering Sea and the narrow sea.

According to a semi-canon source, the Broken Branch is within the dominion of House Manderly. There is ice fishing on the northern rivers.

Fevre River.summary: The Fever River is a river in the southern regions of the north.

Breakwater.summary: Breakwater, also called Breakwater Castle, is a castle which defends the town of Sisterton in the Three Sisters, which are ruled by the Vale of Arryn. The castle is the residence of House Borrell, Lords of Sweetsister and Masters of Breakwater Castle.
facts: House Borrell of Sweetsister, feudal lord

Pebble.summary: Pebble is an island in the Bite north of the Fingers. It is the seat of House Pryor, sworn to the Eyrie.

Sealskin Point.summary: Sealskin Point is the seat of House Farwynd of Sealskin Point on Great Wyk.

Volmark.summary: Volmark is the seat of House Volmark on Harlaw in the Iron Islands.

Straits of Fair Isle.summary: The Straits of Fair Isle lie between the island of Fair Isle and the mainland westerlands.

Nunn's Deep.summary: Nunn's Deep is the site of a gold mine in the westerlands. Its exact location has not been published.

Oxcross.summary: Oxcross is a village not three days ride from Lannisport in the westerlands. It is located near the pass beneath the Golden Tooth, at a fording of the Oxcross.

Red Lake.summary: Red Lake is the seat of House Crane in the Reach. The castle is located on the northeastern shore of a lake of the same name in the northwest of the Reach, near the region's border with the westerlands. Red Lake is northwest of Goldengrove, northeast of Old Oak, and southeast of Cornfield.

Coldmoat.summary: Coldmoat, also called Coldmoat Castle, is a castle of House Webber and House Osgrey in the north-west of the Reach. It is located a few leagues west of Standfast, with the west way running between the two.
facts: Houses Webber and Osgrey, feudal lord

Horseshoe Hills.summary: The Horseshoe Hills are a series of hills in the northwestern Reach. They are part of House Webber's holdings. They once belonged to House Osgrey, after Ser Eustace Osgrey married Lady Rohanne Webber they may or may not belong to House Osgrey once again. They are coveted by Lord Stackhouse.

Brandybottom.summary: Brandybottom is a village in the Reach near Coldmoat and Standfast. It was once under the dominion of House Osgrey, but the power of the house diminished and the control of Brandybottom fell to others.

Dosk.summary: Dosk is a trading village near Standfast in the Reach. It once fell under the dominion of House Osgrey, but the power of the house diminished over the years and the incomes of the village were given to someone else.

Little Dosk.summary: Little Dosk was a village in the Reach. During the reign of King Aerys I Targaryen, it was raided by ironmen and half of the village was destroyed. It was once controlled by House Osgrey, but the power of the house diminished over the years, and the village eventually came under the power of someone else.

Cobble Cove.summary: Cobble Cove is a place in the Reach. It was once the extent of House Osgrey lands.

Hewett's Town.summary: Lord Hewett's Town is a large town on the island of Oakenshield in the Reach. It is the seat of House Hewett.

Leafy Lake.summary: Leafy Lake is a lake in the Reach. It lies within the lands of House Webber. The mouth of the Chequy Water flows into it.

Chequy Water.summary: The Chequy Water is a stream that runs between the lands of House Osgrey and House Webber in the north-western Reach. It rises in the Horseshoe Hills and ends in Leafy Lake. Its underbrush has thorny vines, nettles, and tangles of briarwhite and young willow. The west way crosses the stream.

Grimston.summary: Grimston is a castle on the island of Greyshield in the Reach and is the seat of House Grimm.

Hag's Mire.summary: Hag's Mire is a village in the northern riverlands and the seat of House Nayland. If one intends to go around the Blue Fork, one must pass through Sevenstreams and Hag's Mire, which is considered full of bogs and bad roads. Hag's Mire is full of green pools and soft ground.

Oldstones.summary: Oldstones is the name given by smallfolk to a ruined castle in the northern riverlands. Once the seat of House Mudd, its original name has long been lost.

Sevenstreams.summary: Sevenstreams is a village in the northern riverlands under the jurisdiction of House Frey. If one intends to go around the Blue Fork, one must pass through Sevenstreams and Hag's Mire, which is considered full of bogs and bad roads. The Blue Fork dissolves into smaller waterways such as rills and brooks beyond Sevenstreams. Tom Sevenstrings and Ser Pate of the Blue Fork are cousins from the village.

Ramsford.summary: Ramsford is a village on the Blue Fork of the Trident.

Wendish Town.summary: Wendish Town is a town with in the riverlands. The location of Wendish Town has not yet been revealed by George R. R. Martin. The town may be under the dominion of House Darry as Ser Raymun Darry reports on its status to the Iron Throne. The television adaptations Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon place Wendish Town north of Raventree Hall and south of the source of the Blue Fork.

Mudgrave.summary: Mudgrave is a market town held by House Blackwood in the riverlands.

Pennytree.summary: Pennytree is a large village in the riverlands, located north of the Red Fork in the disputed border area between Stone Hedge and Raventree Hall. The surrounding lands have frequently changed hands in the ongoing conflict between House Bracken and House Blackwood.

Kneeling Man.summary: The Inn of the Kneeling Man is an inn in the riverlands located near the spot where Torrhen Stark, King in the North, is said to have bent the knee to Aegon I Targaryen during Aegon's Conquest.

Sallydance.summary: Sallydance is a small village on the Red Fork in the riverlands. Its sept has windows of leaded glass.

Nutten.summary: Nutten is a settlement near the crossroads inn in the riverlands. Jon O' Nutten comes from the town.

Riverbend.summary: Riverbend is a village near the crossroads inn in the riverlands.

Harroway.summary: Lord Harroway's Town, called Harroway town or Harroway for short, is a town in the riverlands that sits along the Trident, upriver of the ruby ford. It is the seat of House Roote but is named after extinct House Harroway.

Ruby Ford.summary: The ruby ford or Ruby Ford is a crossing of the Trident in the eastern riverlands. It is so named for the rubies that were knocked from Prince Rhaegar Targaryen's breastplate during the Battle of the Trident. The inn at the crossroads lies near the ford. There is no crossing of the Green Fork north of it until the Twins.

Lambswold.summary: Lambswold is a village in the riverlands. It lies near the Inn of the Kneeling Man.

Willow Wood.summary: Willow Wood is the seat of House Ryger in the riverlands.

Stone Mill.summary: Stone Mill, also called the Stone Mill, is a crossing of the Red Fork of the Trident in the western riverlands. The location of Stone Mill has not yet been published on maps, although it may be north of Pinkmaiden Castle.

Lychester.summary: Lord Lychester's keep is the seat of House Lychester in the riverlands. It is three days travel from the hidden village of the Lady of the Leaves, and four days travel from Sallydance.

Atranta.summary: Atranta is the seat of House Vance of Atranta. It is situated in the riverlands.
facts: House Vance of Atranta, feudal lord

Sherrer.summary: Sherrer is a village in the riverlands, downriver from Mummer's Ford on the Red Fork. The village may be under the dominion of House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest, as Ser Karyl Vance reports on its status to the Iron Throne.

High Heart.summary: High Heart is a tall hill sacred to the children of the forest in the riverlands. Around its crown stands a ring of thirty-one weirwood stumps. The hill is considered a safe place due to its relative height compared to the flat surrounding land, making it nearly impossible to be approached unseen.

Acorn Hall.summary: Acorn Hall is the seat of House Smallwood in the riverlands. It is located southeast of Riverrun, northeast of Pinkmaiden, and north of Stoney Sept. High Heart and Blackbottom Bend are nearby.

Wayfarer's Rest.summary: Wayfarer's Rest is the seat of House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest in the riverlands, probably located in the western part of the region near the Red Fork and the border with the westerlands.

Mummer's Ford.summary: The Mummer's Ford is a crossing of the river Trident, along the Red Fork, in the western riverlands. Upriver of Sherrer, it has a town along its banks. The location of the Mummer's Ford has not yet been published on maps, although it may be north of Pinkmaiden Castle.

Rushing Falls.summary: Rushing Falls is the site of one of Lord Beric Dondarrion's many reported deaths. It is located near the Gods Eye in the riverlands.

Crossed Elms.summary: Crossed Elms is a village located west of the Gods Eye in the riverlands. It was the site of a skirmish during the Dance of the Dragons.

Briarwhite.summary: Briarwhite is a holdfast in the southeastern riverlands. It is located west of the kingsroad and east of the Gods Eye river. Briarwhite shares its name with a type of plant that grows along the Chequy Water in the Reach.

Tumbler's Falls.summary: Tumbler's Falls is a town in the southern riverlands. It lies on the Blackwater Rush.

Widow's Ford.summary: The Widow's Ford is a ford in the riverlands, possibly near Darry.

Saltpans.summary: Saltpans is a town in the riverlands that sits on the Bay of Crabs. It is the seat of House Cox, although semi-canon sources indicate that House Hawick is also from the town.

Quiet Isle.summary: The Quiet Isle is an upthrust island that sits at the mouth of the Trident where it flows into the Bay of Crabs, southeast of Saltpans and northwest of Maidenpool. Its septry is a refuge for those sworn to the Faith of the Seven. Septon Meribald has often visited the isle.

Gods Eye River.summary: The Gods Eye river is a river in the southern riverlands and western crownlands. The river's name is not published in A Clash of Kings.

Field of Fire.summary: The Field of Fire was a major battle during Aegon I Targaryen's war of conquest. According to semi-canon sources the field is located in the northern part of the Reach.
facts: Northern Reach, south of the Blackwater Rush and near the Goldroad
Targaryen victory, Extinction of House Gardener, Submission of House Lannister

Redgrass Field.summary:
The Redgrass Field is the site of the Battle of the Redgrass Field. It was an unnamed field before the battle. It was renamed the Redgrass Field after the battle for the color grass had been stained by the blood.

While its exact location has not yet been confirmed, the Redgrass Field is known to be located somewhere near King's Landing.

The Northmarch.summary: Marshal of the Northmarch is a title once held by the head of House Osgrey; the Osgreys defended the northern regions of the Kingdom of the Reach.

New Barrel.summary: New Barrel is the seat of House Fossoway of New Barrel. The castle is located in the Reach. Its name suggests it may be involved in the production of cider, like Cider Hall is for the elder branch of the family.

Appleton.summary: Appleton is the seat of House Appleton in the Reach.

Cider Hall.summary: Cider Hall is the seat of House Fossoway of Cider Hall in the Reach. It is located near the confluence of the Cockleswhent and the Mander. The castle is named after the alcoholic beverage.

Grassfield Keep.summary: Grassfield Keep is the castle of House Meadows in or near the town of Grassy Vale in the Reach.

Grassy Vale.summary: Grassy Vale is a town controlled by House Meadows in the Reach. It sits along the northern shore of the Blueburn river, close to the border with the stormlands. Grassfield Keep, the castle of Lord Elwood Meadows, is located in or near Grassy Vale.

Griffin's Roost.summary: Griffin's Roost, or simply the Roost, is the seat of House Connington in the stormlands. The castle is located between Storm's End and Crow's Nest in northwestern Cape Wrath. It is ruled by Ser Ronnet Connington, the Knight of Griffin's Roost.
facts: Ser Ronnet Connington (ACoK), Lord Jon Connington (ADwD)

Gates of the Moon.summary: The Gates of the Moon, also known as the Gates, is a castle at the base of the Giant's Lance in the Vale of Arryn. It is held by Lord Nestor Royce, High Steward of the Vale and Keeper of the Gates of the Moon, on behalf of House Arryn.
facts: House Arryn & House Royce, Feudal lord
Lord Nestor Royce (keeper for House Arryn)
Great Hall, East Tower, Falcon Tower

Giant's Lance.summary: The Giant's Lance is the tallest peak of the Mountains of the Moon within the Vale of Arryn, extending three and a half miles above the valley below.

Heart's Home.summary: Heart's Home is a castle in the Vale of Arryn and is the seat of House Corbray, a vassal house holding fealty to House Arryn of the Eyrie. It is located on the northern shore where a glacial river flows into a narrow bay of the narrow sea. Upriver to the west is Strongsong, while directly north is a forest. Snakewood is located to the northeast along the bay, while the Eyrie is south across a mountain range.
facts: Seat of House Corbray, Feudal society

Crackclaw Point.summary:
Crackclaw Point, also called Crackclaw or the Point, is a peninsula in the crownlands jutting out into the narrow sea. To the north lies the Bay of Crabs, to the south Blackwater Bay. Maidenpool and Rook's Rest are west of the forested peninsula, while Dragonstone and Claw Isle are to the south and east, respectively.

Noble houses from Crackclaw Point include House Boggs, House Brune of Brownhollow, House Brune of the Dyre Den, House Cave, House Crabb (formerly of the Whispers), House Hardy, and House Pyne.

The Whispers.summary: The Whispers is a ruined castle of House Crabb on Crackclaw Point in the northeastern crownlands.

Hull.summary: Hull is a town on the island of Driftmark in the crownlands. It is located beneath the walls of Castle Driftmark on the north side of the isle, opposite Spicetown on the south side. "Hull" took its name from the rows of ship hulls at anchor below the castle.
facts: Lord Monford Velaryon (AGoT), Lord Monterys Velaryon (ADwD)

Spicetown.summary: Spicetown or Spice-town was a town on the island of Driftmark in the crownlands. It was located near High Tide, athwart the Gullet.
facts: 130 AC, during the Dance of the Dragons

High Tide.summary: High Tide is one of the castles of House Velaryon on the island of Driftmark in the crownlands.

Sweetport.summary: Sweetport Sound is the seat of House Sunglass in the crownlands. Sweetport Sound is sworn to Dragonstone, although its location along Blackwater Bay or the narrow sea has not been revealed. Ser Triston of Tally Hill is sworn to Lord Guncer Sunglass, so Tally Hill may be located near Sweetport Sound.

Rambton.summary: House Rambton is a noble house from the crownlands. They blazon their arms with a white ram's head with golden horns on red.
facts: A white ram's head with golden horns on red, (Gules, a ram's head cabossed argent attired or)

Evenfall Hall.summary: Evenfall Hall, or simply Evenfall, is the seat of House Tarth in the stormlands. It is located on the western coast of the island of Tarth along Shipbreaker Bay.

Wickenden.summary: Wickenden is the seat of House Waxley in the Vale of Arryn. The town is on the northern shore of the Bay of Crabs, northwest of Crackclaw Point. It is famous for making scented beeswax candles.

Bandallon.summary: Bandallon is the seat of House Blackbar in the Reach. It is located on the shores of the Sunset Sea, west of Brightwater Keep, northwest of Oldtown, and southwest of the Shield Islands.

Brightwater Keep.summary: Brightwater Keep, also known as Brightwater, is the seat of House Florent in the Reach. It sits near the source of the Honeywine, north of Honeyholt, east of Bandallon, and southwest of the Mander.
facts: House Tyrell of Brightwater Keep/House Florent, feudal lord
Lord Alester Florent (ACoK), Lord Garlan Tyrell (ADwD)

Honeyholt.summary: Honeyholt is the seat of House Beesbury in the Reach. It is situated along the eastern bank of the Honeywine river between Brightwater Keep and Oldtown.

Uplands.summary: Uplands is the seat of House Mullendore in the Reach. It is located east of Oldtown and west of the Red Mountains, along a river which flows west to the Honeywine.

Blackcrown.summary:
Blackcrown is the seat of House Bulwer in the southwestern Reach. It is located on the northern shore of Whispering Sound near Oldtown and Three Towers.

The cliffs near Blackcrown are called singing cliffs for the whistle heard from the twisted towers and wind-carved stones standing above the waves.

Blackcrown's maester is Normund.

Three Towers.summary: Three Towers is the seat of House Costayne in the Reach. It sits on a cliff on the southern shore of Whispering Sound, almost where the sound meets the Redwyne Straits.

Mouth of the Mander.summary: The Mander is a river in the Reach which flows past Highgarden, the seat of House Tyrell. It is the longest and broadest river in the Seven Kingdoms. The Tyrells include Lord Paramount of the Mander among their titles.

Mermaid's Palace.summary: Mermaid's Palace is a small isle off the coast of the Arbor.

Starfish Harbor.summary: Starfish Harbor is a town with a port that sits along the Redwyne Straits in the Arbor.

Ryamsport.summary:
Ryamsport is a town with a port on the Arbor.

It is possibly named after Ryam Redwyne, famed Lord Commander of the Kingsguard under kings Jaehaerys I and Viserys I Targaryen.

Vinetown.summary: Vinetown is a town with a port that sits along the Redwyne Straits on the Arbor.

Isle of Pigs.summary: The Isle of Pigs is a small isle off the coast of the Arbor, possibly the seat of House Farrow.

Cuy.summary: Cuy is a town which lies outside the walls of Sunhouse in the Reach. Cuy and Sunhouse are located along the southern shore of the Reach and are ruled by House Cuy.

Dunstonbury.summary: Dunstonbury is a castle in the Reach. Its current ruling house has not been published.

Horn Hill.summary: Horn Hill is the seat of House Tarly in the Reach. Located on an eponymous hill, the castle lies south of Highgarden and a hundred leagues northeast of Oldtown among the thickly-wooded foothills of the Red Mountains. The Tarlys are marcher lords of the Dornish Marches.
facts: Age of Heroes by Herndon of the Horn and Harlon the Hunter

Ashford.summary: Ashford, also called Ashford Castle, is the seat of House Ashford in the Reach. The castle and its town sit on the northern shore of a fording of the Cockleswent, north of the Dornish Marches.

Ashford Meadow.summary: Ashford Meadow is a grassy field on the southern shore of the Cockleswent in the Reach, across the river from Ashford. In normal times the meadow serves as a commons for smallfolk.

Whitegrove.summary: Whitegrove is a castle in the Reach. Its current ruling house has not been published.

Starpike.summary: Starpike is the seat of House Peake in the Reach. The castle may be located in the Dornish Marches.

Harvest Hall.summary: Harvest Hall is the seat of House Selmy in the Dornish Marches, in the stormlands. According to a semi-canon source, it is located near the eastern border of the Reach, northeast of Nightsong, northwest of Blackhaven and south of the Cockleswhent.

Vulture's Roost.summary: Vulture's Roost is a ruined castle in northern Dorne. It lies near the source of the Wyl river deep in the Red Mountains.

High Hermitage.summary: High Hermitage is the seat of House Dayne of High Hermitage. It is located in the Red Mountains of Dorne, northeast of Starfall.

Torrentine.summary: The Torrentine or Torentine is a river in western Dorne.

Hellgate Hall.summary: Hellgate Hall was the seat of House Dryland, who ruled as Kings of the Brimstone in Dorne prior to Nymeria's War. It is unknown what happened to the castle after the defeat of King Lucifer Dryland, as he was the last of his line.

Slayne.summary: The Slayne is a river in Cape Wrath in the stormlands. Known for its rapids, pools, and waterfalls, the Slayne flows south from the northeastern Red Mountains to the Sea of Dorne.

King's Mountain.summary: King's Mountain is a place in the Seven Kingdoms; its location has not been revealed.

Crow's Nest.summary: Crow's Nest is the seat of House Morrigen in the stormlands. It is located in mountainous terrain between Griffin's Roost and Stonehelm, along the western edge of Cape Wrath and the rainwood.

Stonehelm.summary: Stonehelm is a castle in the stormlands and is the ancient seat of House Swann. The castle is situated in the Red Watch region of the eastern Dornish Marches, on Cape Wrath along the coast of the Sea of Dorne.

The Red Watch.summary: The Red Watch is the region around Stonehelm in the southern stormlands, where the Red Mountains meet Cape Wrath. It is part of the eastern Dornish Marches and is ruled by House Swann, marcher lords who historically defended against incursions from Dorne or the Reach.

Fawnton.summary: Fawnton is the seat of House Cafferen in the stormlands. The precise location of Fawnton is unknown.

Mistwood.summary: Mistwood or Mistfall is the seat of House Mertyns in the stormlands. It is located in the southern rainwood in Cape Wrath.

Weeping Town.summary:
The Weeping Town is a market town in the stormlands. Lying on the southern shore of Cape Wrath, along the Sea of Dorne, it has a thriving port which handles much of the stormlands' trade. It contains a seat, possibly known as the Weeping Tower. It is ruled by House Whitehead.

The town has stout wooden walls, peaked roofs, and crooked alleys. It is large enough to support three inns: the Broken Shield, the Loon, and the Drunken Dornishman.

Roost.summary: Griffin's Roost, or simply the Roost, is the seat of House Connington in the stormlands. The castle is located between Storm's End and Crow's Nest in northwestern Cape Wrath. It is ruled by Ser Ronnet Connington, the Knight of Griffin's Roost.
facts: Ser Ronnet Connington (ACoK), Lord Jon Connington (ADwD)

Rain House.summary: Rain House, also called the Rain House, is the seat of House Wylde in the stormlands. It sits in the eastern rainwood along the southern shore of Shipbreaker Bay near the northeastern tip of Cape Wrath.

Greenstone.summary: Greenstone is the seat of House Estermont on the island of Estermont in the stormlands.

Water Gardens.summary: The Water Gardens is a palace with gardens and waterworks that serves as a private retreat to House Martell, the rulers of Dorne.

Last Lament.summary: Last Lament is a town in northwestern Walano in the Summer Isles. To the north of it is the island Stone Head.

Lorath Island.summary: Lorath is one of the Nine Free Cities. It is in a group of islands in the Shivering Sea, near the northern coast of Essos.
facts: Council of three princes (nominally), Council of magisters

The Tree of Crowns.summary: The Tree of Crowns is located in the Disputed Lands. In 258 AC, nine outlaws, exiles, pirates, and sellsword captains—remembered by history as the "Band of Nine"—met beneath the Tree of Crowns as to form an alliance, swearing to aid each other in conquering kingdoms for each of the nine members.

Kyth.summary: Kyth is a ruined city in Essos in the Dothraki sea, in the Kingdom of Sarnor. It was located near where the Sarne turned north. Kyth and Hornoth were destroyed by rival Dothraki khals after the fall of Sallosh.

Vaes Gorqoyi.summary: Vaes Gorqoyi is a ruined city in Essos in the Dothraki sea, in the Kingdom of Sarnor. Named Mardosh by the Tall Men, it was known as the "City of Soldiers" and Mardosh the Unconquerable.

Hornoth.summary: Hornoth is a ruined city in Essos in the Dothraki sea, in the Kingdom of Sarnor. It was located near where the Sarne turned north. Hornoth and Kyth were destroyed by rival Dothraki khals after the fall of Sallosh.

Rathylar.summary: Rathylar is a ruined city in Essos in the Dothraki sea, in the Kingdom of Sarnor. It was located near where the Sarne turned north. As Saath is the only Sarnori city to have survived the Century of Blood, Rathylar was presumably destroyed by the Dothraki as well.

The Sarne.summary: The Sarne is a river in northern Essos located east of the Forest of Qohor and north of the Painted Mountains.

The Qhoyne.summary:
The Qhoyne is a river in northwestern Essos. The Rhoynar consider it a daughter of the Rhoyne and nickname it the Darkling Daughter. Its headwaters lie in the Forest of Qohor, where it runs through the Free City of Qohor. It then flows southwest past the forest and meets its tributary, the south-flowing Darkwash, just north of the ruined city of Ar Noy. The Qhoyne then continues southwest past Ar Noy and meets the Rhoyne at Dagger Lake.

Pine-cones from the Forest of Qohor and gold and amber from the Axe flow into Dagger Lake by way of the Qhoyne and the Darkwash, respectively. Timber from the forest is shipped to the southern Rhoyne via the Qhoyne and Dagger Lake.

Barter Beach.summary: Barter Beach is a market of sorts on Talon, one of the Basilisk Isles. It is where the corsairs of the isles go to trade among themselves.

Talon.summary: Talon is a warship in service to the Night's Watch at Eastwatch-by-the-Sea. The galley's rowers sit on an open deck. Its captain is Ser Maynard Holt.

Field of Crows.summary: The Field of Crows was the largest battle between the Dothraki and the Tall Men during the Century of Blood. The victory of the horselords allowed them to conquer the rest of the Kingdom of Sarnor.

Lonely Hill.summary: The Lonely Hills are a series of hills controlled by House Umber in the north. They lie east of Long Lake, south of the Last River and the Last Hearth, and northwest of the Dreadfort.

Howling Mountain.summary: The Howling Mountain is one of the Basilisk Isles, which are off the northern coast of Sothoryos.

Lower Zamoyos.summary: The Zamoyos is a river in Sothoryos which flows into the Summer Sea at a large delta. It is known for its green waters, quicksands, and rotting, half-submerged trees. The river contains crocodiles, schools of carnivorous fish, and worms which lay eggs in swimmers.

Upper Zamoyos.summary: The Zamoyos is a river in Sothoryos which flows into the Summer Sea at a large delta. It is known for its green waters, quicksands, and rotting, half-submerged trees. The river contains crocodiles, schools of carnivorous fish, and worms which lay eggs in swimmers.

Marahai Bay.summary:
Marahai is a crescent-shaped island in the central Jade Sea, off the southern coast of Essos. West of Marahai are Great Moraq, the Isle of Whips, and the Isle of Elephants. Additionally, Leng and the Manticore Isles are east of Marahai. The city of Yin in Yi Ti is to the north across the Jade Sea.

Marahai is called a paradise isle. Within its curvature are two small volcanic isles which often emit smoke and flame.

Ash.summary: Ash is one of the children of the forest in service to the last greenseer. Their true name is too long for the human tongue, according to Leaf.

Westeros.summary: Westeros is one of the three known continents in the known world, the others being Essos and Sothoryos. Most of the area of Westeros is covered by a political entity known as the Seven Kingdoms, while the far north beyond the Wall includes the free folk. The closest foreign nations to Westeros are the Free Cities, a collection of independent city-states across the narrow sea in western Essos. To the south of Westeros lie the Summer Isles.

Essos.summary:
Essos, often simply called the east, is the largest of the three known continents in the world. It lies east of Westeros and north of Sothoryos and Ulthos, stretching from the Shivering Sea in the north to the Summer Sea in the south, and from the narrow sea in the west to the lands surrounding the Jade Sea in the east, if not farther. Essos is populated by many different peoples and has a vast and varied geography.

In the novels of A Song of Ice and Fire, the continent is simply called the eastern continent, beyond the narrow sea, or the east; George R. R. Martin first referred to it as Essos in mid-2008 in an interview, and later officially confirmed it. The Appendix of A Dance with Dragons officially refers to the continent east of the narrow sea as Essos.
